inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,916 logical lines. The source develops Robin's normalized divisor-sum criterion into the record sequence XA, supplies analytic tools for SA/CA/XA comparisons, proves structural and asymptotic results, and closes with explicitly finite numerical observations. Displayed mathematics is generally recoverable from the text layer, although several composite-function displays and long inequality chains remain formula-layout dependent.

sections_inspected.label: Title, abstract, and source metadata
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Front matter and a duplicate high-level statement of the XA/RH criterion.

sections_inspected.label: 1 Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the Robin normalization, situates Gronwall and related criteria, and motivates restricting a least counterexample to record-setting divisor-sum sequences.

sections_inspected.label: 2 Extremely abundant numbers
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines XA, relates it to SA, localizes a least Robin counterexample, and proves the infinitude criterion equivalent to RH.

sections_inspected.label: 3 Auxiliary Lemmas
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Builds perturbation, logarithmic-growth, Chebyshev-function, prime-counting, oscillation, prime-gap, and Euler-product estimates used later.

sections_inspected.label: 4 Superabundant-number properties
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives spacing, exponent, largest-prime, asymptotic divisor-sum, and monotonicity properties along SA.

sections_inspected.label: 4 Colossally abundant-number properties
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Parameterizes CA numbers, gives their endpoint-envelope role for f, transfers XA records to CA endpoints, and uses Chebyshev oscillation to separate prime and logarithmic scales infinitely often.

sections_inspected.label: 4 Extremely abundant-number properties
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bounds the largest prime factor of XA, separates XA from infinitely many CA numbers, and proves a conditional monotonicity statement along consecutive XA numbers.

sections_inspected.label: 5 Numerical experiments
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Reports finite-range exponent, ordering, spacing, ratio, set-overlap, and arithmetic-function monotonicity observations with explicit cutoffs.

sections_inspected.label: Acknowledgments and references
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Non-unit-bearing back matter and bibliographic provenance.

accepted_units.title: Robin normalization and record-sequence counterexample sieve
accepted_units.why_material: Connects the pointwise Robin inequality with Gronwall's limiting upper envelope and explains why a least violation can be sought among superabundant record setters, while contrasting other divisor-function formulations.
accepted_units.context_note: The span contains the definition of f, the Robin and Gronwall statements, and the motivation for the later XA refinement; the trailing extraordinary-number criterion is included as a nearby comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose is coherent; displayed formulas for f and the criteria must be retained, but their symbols are legible in the normalized text.

accepted_units.title: Extremely abundant records and an infinitude criterion for RH
accepted_units.why_material: Defines XA as successive records of f above a fixed baseline, proves XA is contained in SA, places any least Robin counterexample in XA, and proves RH iff XA is infinite by combining record behavior with Gronwall's limsup.
accepted_units.context_note: The section heading at line 168 should accompany this immutable v1 span in downstream presentation; the mathematical definition and both directions of the criterion are inside the span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The argument depends on displayed ratios and inequalities, all recoverable from the normalized extraction.

accepted_units.title: Inverting relative logarithmic perturbations
accepted_units.why_material: Provides a reusable mechanism for converting a two-sided relative bound on y around x into a two-sided relative bound on x around y with controlled logarithmic error constants.
accepted_units.context_note: The full lemma and proof are kept because the transformed constants are not intelligible from the statement alone.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula layout is important; the normalized inequalities are readable but should be rendered from structured mathematics when reused.

accepted_units.title: Controlling changes in x log log x
accepted_units.why_material: Packages monotonicity of a normalized secant ratio for x log log x and a square-root comparison for log-log growth, later enabling consecutive-record monotonicity arguments.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes inequality (3.1), whose elementary derivation supplies the explicit perturbation term used later with a bounded ratio of consecutive SA numbers.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose identifies the functions, but the exact normalized ratio and inequality require the displayed formulas.

accepted_units.title: Effective Chebyshev and prime-counting bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Collects explicit two-sided estimates for theta and psi and bounds for pi, including how cited estimates plus finite computation produce constants usable in later largest-prime arguments.
accepted_units.context_note: The long calculations are retained as certification logic for the stated ranges; they depend on cited external theorems rather than being derived from first principles here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several radicals, thresholds, and error constants are display-layout sensitive, though the conclusions and range conditions are recoverable from the text layer.

accepted_units.title: Oscillation, prime steps, and Mertens-product control
accepted_units.why_material: Supplies sign-changing theta/psi oscillation, a short-interval prime input, a bound on consecutive primes, and explicit Euler-product estimates that drive later CA separation and XA monotonicity arguments.
accepted_units.context_note: These are cited auxiliary results rather than proofs; their distinct roles are preserved together as the source's analytic toolkit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The omega-plus/minus scale and product bounds require faithful mathematical rendering; the normalized symbols are sufficiently recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Dense SA records force lower bounds on prime exponents
accepted_units.why_material: Shows consecutive SA numbers differ by at most a factor of two and uses a replacement competitor to force each prime exponent to be at least the floor of log p divided by log q.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the local SA definition and both short proofs, making the competitor construction self-contained.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The multiplicative comparison involving replacing p by a power of q is formula dependent but legible.

accepted_units.title: Prime-power balance in SA factorizations
accepted_units.why_material: Relates exponents at different primes and derives two-sided scale control of the power of two by p log p, exposing the compressed exponent profile of superabundant integers.
accepted_units.context_note: Some inputs are quoted from Alaoglu-Erdos; the corollaries and their use of logarithmic inequalities are explicit in the source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equations (4.2)-(4.5) have dense fractions and error terms; their exact symbolic layout must be preserved.

accepted_units.title: From the exponent profile to p asymptotic to log n
accepted_units.why_material: Combines the two-adic scale, the known SA relation p asymptotic to log n, and Chebyshev sums to sandwich log n relative to theta(p), clarifying how factorization geometry controls the ambient size.
accepted_units.context_note: The span ends after the preparatory theta comparison; the explicit final inequalities are carried in the following immutable v1 unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The proof of Proposition 4.12 and Lemma 4.14 contains OCR-sensitive summations and radicals, but the theorem statements and argument structure are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Effective approach of SA divisor sums to the Gronwall constant
accepted_units.why_material: Uses explicit p-versus-log n bounds, a comparison of sigma(n)/n with n/phi(n), and an Euler product to prove f(n) tends to e^gamma along SA with a quantitative lower bound.
accepted_units.context_note: This immutable v1 span needs the preceding exponent and Chebyshev setup to avoid treating its largest-prime bounds as unexplained inputs.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed product inequalities and asymptotic bounds are essential; they are readable, though formula-aware rendering is advisable.

accepted_units.title: Additive excess sigma(n) minus n increases along SA
accepted_units.why_material: Extracts an additive monotonic quantity directly from the defining multiplicative record property of SA, illustrating a reusable conversion from ratio growth to difference growth.
accepted_units.context_note: The statement and complete comparison proof are self-contained.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Minimal; the displayed chain is legible in text.

accepted_units.title: Exponentiating record growth preserves an SA monotone
accepted_units.why_material: Combines SA ratio growth with the additive excess monotonicity to prove increase of a nonlinear sigma(n)-exponent expression.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a distinct representation lift of the preceding mechanism rather than a repeated statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The definition and proof are highly display-layout dependent, and the normalized extraction should be checked against the rendered formula before training use.

accepted_units.title: Monotonicity after subtracting n log log n
accepted_units.why_material: Uses bounded spacing of consecutive SA numbers, log-log secant control, and the asymptotic lower bound for sigma to show an adjusted additive excess increases, then lifts that result to a nonlinear normalized expression.
accepted_units.context_note: The two statements share the same comparison mechanism and are retained together with the complete inequality chain.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The second nonlinear expression and equations (4.14)-(4.15) are OCR-layout sensitive; use requires formula verification despite coherent prose.

accepted_units.title: Transferring SA growth through phi and Psi
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how monotone prime support controls n/phi(n) and combines that support change with SA growth to derive further monotonic arithmetic-function expressions.
accepted_units.context_note: The sequence assumption is explicit; the final Psi-exponent formula is included because it represents a separate transfer construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The final displayed powers are degraded by text extraction and require verification from a typeset rendering before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Threshold coordinates for CA prime exponents
accepted_units.why_material: Represents a CA number through a parameter epsilon and threshold values x_k, turning the global extremal inequality into local exponent intervals and explaining uniqueness or finite multiplicity at boundary parameters.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the exceptional case where threshold values are prime and the resulting two-or-four possible CA numbers.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Products (4.19)-(4.21) and boundary inclusions are essential and formula-layout dependent, but the prose recovers their meaning.

accepted_units.title: CA endpoints capture maxima of the Robin normalization
accepted_units.why_material: States that between successive CA numbers the normalized divisor sum cannot exceed both endpoint values, reducing the search for Robin violations to CA endpoints.
accepted_units.context_note: The result is quoted from Robin and immediately interpreted; no proof is given in this source.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Minimal beyond the displayed max inequality.

accepted_units.title: Transferring XA records to CA endpoints and exploiting theta oscillation
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that an XA point between successive CA numbers forces the upper CA endpoint into XA, derives infinitely many CA∩XA under RH, and then constructs infinitely many CA numbers with largest prime exceeding log N from Chebyshev oscillation.
accepted_units.context_note: This immutable v1 span requires the preceding CA parameterization and endpoint-envelope theorem to make both the transfer and the oscillatory construction locally grounded.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The square-root oscillation scale and the parameter relation F(p,1) must be preserved in mathematical notation.

accepted_units.title: XA records force p below log n
accepted_units.why_material: Compares an XA number with n/p and converts the record inequality through a logarithmic bound to prove its largest prime factor is strictly below log n.
accepted_units.context_note: The proof uses a finite check to ensure n/p remains above the XA baseline; the surrounding subsection label should accompany presentation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The key ratio and logarithmic implication are legible but formula dependent.

accepted_units.title: Prime-scale incompatibility yields infinitely many CA outside XA
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts the XA prime bound with the preceding infinite CA family having p greater than log N, yielding an unconditional infinite separation of the two extremal classes.
accepted_units.context_note: The cited t-free analogue is a comparison; Theorem 4.34 itself is an immediate synthesis of Theorems 4.31 and 4.32.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Minimal; the key inequalities are stated in prose and simple display.

accepted_units.title: A spacing condition makes (sigma+phi)/n increase along XA
accepted_units.why_material: Combines XA record growth, explicit product estimates, a prime-gap bound, and a lower spacing assumption to prove monotonicity of a mixed divisor-totient statistic for consecutive XA numbers.
accepted_units.context_note: The source reports that the hypotheses were checked only through the 8150th XA element; that finite observation is not part of the theorem's proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The multi-line lower-bound chain is OCR-fragile and must be checked against the typeset formula before exact reuse.

accepted_units.title: Observed local rigidity of XA exponent vectors
accepted_units.why_material: Records finite-range relations among adjacent prime-power blocks, one-step exponent changes between consecutive XA numbers, monotone largest-prime and divisor-count observations, and counterexamples showing these patterns do not automatically characterize highly composite or SA behavior.
accepted_units.context_note: All claims are empirical within the stated C1 cutoff and rely on an external list of SA numbers; they must not be promoted to universal theorems.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Primorial factorizations and exponent notation are recoverable but should retain typeset structure.

accepted_units.title: Empirical overlap of XA and CA below a fixed SA cutoff
accepted_units.why_material: Quantifies that neither XA nor CA contains the other in the inspected finite domain and measures the substantial but non-identical overlap.
accepted_units.context_note: The cutoff is C equal to the millionth superabundant number; the counts are dataset-dependent finite evidence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Minimal; set-difference notation must be preserved.

accepted_units.title: Computed spacing, ratio, and composition monotonicities
accepted_units.why_material: Provides a concentrated bank of finite-range structural hypotheses on consecutive SA/XA spacing and on monotonicity of composed arithmetic functions, suitable for later falsification or theorem selection.
accepted_units.context_note: Every property is bounded by C2 or an explicitly stated domain; the source gives observations, not proofs, and the table immediately before this span is only illustrative data.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Many floor, composition, and exponent displays are extraction-sensitive; exact formulas require typeset verification before reuse.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Record maxima as a two-level Robin counterexample sieve
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A least Robin violation is forced into the finer XA record sequence, while any violation is also witnessed at a CA endpoint; the XA record process is infinite exactly under RH.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: These reductions do not establish a violation or prove that every XA number is CA; the endpoint and record arguments have different quantifiers.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: CA endpoints transfer XA fertility under RH
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: If RH supplies infinitely many XA records, the CA endpoint envelope maps each intervening XA record to a CA endpoint that is also XA, producing infinitely many members of CA intersect XA.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The infinitude conclusion is conditional on RH through the infinitude of XA and does not imply eventual equality of the sequences.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Prime-scale incompatibility separates CA from XA
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Chebyshev oscillation produces infinitely many CA numbers with p(N) greater than log N, whereas every XA number has p(n) less than log n, so infinitely many CA numbers cannot be XA.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This separates one infinite CA subsequence only; it does not characterize all of CA minus XA or decide RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Factorization geometry bridges SA to the Gronwall scale
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Constraints on SA prime exponents locate the largest prime near log n and make the Euler-product comparison strong enough to drive f(n) toward e^gamma along SA.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The conclusion is asymptotic along SA and supplies no eventual sign for Robin's strict inequality.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Finite XA regularity as a falsifiable conjecture family
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The proved conditional monotonicity and the computed one-step exponent, spacing, ratio, and composition patterns suggest a coordinated local rigidity program for consecutive XA numbers.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Most parents here are finite computations with fixed cutoffs and external-list dependence; they are hypothesis generators, not universal evidence.
